scope: guardian descendant ownership and cleanup after leader exit or SIGKILL
PID namespace mapping and unintended signal target risk
bounded related observation on live descendant measurement

findings.state: FOUND_IN_REVIEWED_SNAPSHOT; owner reports caller-depth fix, not yet independently read back
findings.location: child_snapshot lines415-418 and kill_snapshot lines429-431 in reviewed snapshot
findings.problem: NSpid[-1] identifies the deepest namespace of each descendant. A deeper descendant namespace makes this different from the caller-local PID accepted by os.kill. Validation reads one outer procfs process, but the signal may target a different process in the caller namespace.
necessary_conditions: Read the caller NSpid vector using the same procfs mount. Let d be its length.
Require caller NSpid[-1] equals getpid and caller first entry equals /proc/self/stat PID.
For a proven descendant require target vector length at least d and target first entry equal the observed outer procfs PID.
Map the signal PID as target NSpid[d-1], with valid positive integer identity, rather than target[-1].
If NSpid is unavailable or malformed, do not silently apply a cross-namespace fallback. Accept a direct numeric fallback only when own procfs PID equals getpid and ownership is proven.

findings.problem: The procfs starttime check and subsequent numeric os.kill are separate operations. A process can exit and have its PID recycled between them. Rechecking starttime/local PID narrows but does not atomically close this race.
findings.recommended_resolution: Use a stable process reference when signaling, such as pidfd_send_signal with a procfs process directory fd. Bind identity/ownership reads to the same fd and never convert a validated fd back into a bare PID for the final signal. Report unsupported capability as a bounded cleanup hold; do not silently claim race-free cleanup with kill(PID).
findings.limitation: No PID-reuse schedule was executed; this is the ordinary API race documented by Linux man-pages.

findings.location: build_r3o_rust.py proc_children lines67-80 and live_usage lines83-95
findings.problem: The fast path reads only /proc/PID/task/PID/children. Children forked by other threads can be absent while the parent lives because /proc/.../task/TID/children is per task. The PPid fallback only runs when that main-thread interface is absent.
findings.implication: This can make live CPU/RSS measurement partial. After the leader is terminated, subreaper adoption can still permit eventual cleanup; that does not retroactively establish live measurement coverage.
findings.possible_resolution: Establish the catalog restriction explicitly, or enumerate all task/TID children with de-duplication / use a complete PPid scan for the R3S process tracker.

source_flow_observations: The reviewed guardian calls PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER before spawning the job and loops wait4(-1,WNOHANG).
A leader exit with surviving/adopted descendants produces HOLD and enters cleanup; cleanup is not dependent on process-group membership, so setsid alone does not escape that ownership path.
Controller enables subreaper and rejects direct adopted descendants outside the active guardian inventory, entering cleanup after a guardian hard exit.
These are source-flow observations, not new runtime test PASS claims.
